# Half-mass with two negative exponential coefficients

Let E_0,E_1,...,E_k,E_* be independent standard exponential variables.
Suppose 0<=c<=1, 0<=p_i<=1, and sum_i p_i=1+c. Then

    P(sum_i p_i E_i >= E_0+c E_*) >= 1/2.               (1)

The number k is arbitrary. This is an all-dimensional sign-pattern
lemma, not a bound for arbitrary numbers of negative coefficients.

Assume first 0<c<1, and put

    A=product_i(1+p_i),
    B=product_i(c+p_i),
    L=1/A-c^(k+1)/B.

The survival function of E_0+cE_* and the elementary Laplace transforms
give the exact probability 1-L/(1-c). Thus it suffices to show that L
is maximized over the box/sum constraint at (1,c,0,...,0).

Write R(x)=(c+x)/(1+x). Its logarithm is increasing and concave on
[0,1], since

    (log R)'=1/(c+x)-1/(1+x)>0,
    (log R)''=-1/(c+x)^2+1/(1+x)^2<0.

Whenever two coordinates lie strictly between zero and one, transfer
mass from the smaller to the larger until one reaches an endpoint.
Concavity makes the sum of their log R values decrease. After finitely
many such transfers, at most one coordinate is interior. The sum
constraint identifies the final vector as (1,c,0,...,0), up to
permutation. Consequently every permitted vector satisfies

    B/A=product_i R(p_i)>=R(1)R(c)c^(k-2)=c^(k-1).       (2)

All products are positive. Direct differentiation gives

    partial_i L-partial_j L
      =(p_i-p_j)[1/(A(1+p_i)(1+p_j))
                 -c^(k+1)/(B(c+p_i)(c+p_j))].          (3)

The bracket is nonnegative: by (2),

    (B/A) R(p_i)R(p_j) >= c^(k-1)*c^2=c^(k+1).

Thus the same transfer of mass from a smaller coordinate to a larger
one makes L increase. Repeating until the endpoint vector shows that
its maximum occurs at (1,c,0,...,0). At that vector, the positive and
negative random sums are independent with the same continuous law,
so the probability is exactly 1/2. This proves (1).

If c=0, conditioning on the positive sum gives probability
1-1/product_i(1+p_i)>=1/2, since sum_i p_i=1. If c=1, replace c by
1-epsilon and each p_i by (1-epsilon/2)p_i. These parameters satisfy
the required constraints and converge to the original ones. Coupling
the same exponential variables gives almost-sure convergence of the
inequality indicators off a null equality event; bounded convergence
passes (1) to the limit. Zero coefficients require no separate limit.

In the low-maximum simplex formulation, this proves a half-volume
centroid cap whenever the centered coefficients have at most two
negative entries, one being the mandatory coefficient -1. The family
with several negative entries remains outside this lemma.
